text: attention in mathemtics visualization for LLM

Given: Four tokens: \(n=4\)., Key dimension: \(d_k=2\)., Query: \(q_1=\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix}\)., Keys: \(k_1=(1,0),\ k_2=(2,1),\ k_3=(1,1),\ k_4=(-1,0)\)., Values: \(v_1=(1,0),\ v_2=(2,1),\ v_3=(-1,1),\ v_4=(0,-1)\).
Find: The attention weights for the first query and the resulting attended representation \(z_1\).

1. Choose a small numerical self-attention example
   n=4, dₖ=2
   Use four tokens and two-dimensional query, key, and value vectors. We will calculate the attention output for the first token, whose query is \(q_1\).

2. Specify the query, keys, and values
   q₁=begin bmatrix1\\0end bmatrix, K=begin bmatrix1&0\\2&1\\1&1\\-1&0end bmatrix, V=begin bmatrix1&0\\2&1\\-1&1\\0&-1end bmatrix
   The first row gives the query for the token being updated. Each row of \(K\) is a key belonging to one of the four tokens, and each row of \(V\) is the corresponding value vector.

3. Compute query-key similarity scores
   q₁Kᵀ=begin bmatrix1&2&1&-1end bmatrix
   Take the dot product of the query with each key. For example, \(q_1\cdot k_2=(1)(2)+(0)(1)=2\). Repeating this for all four keys gives the raw similarity scores \(1,2,1,-1\).

4. Scale the scores by the key dimension
   widetilde s=frac q₁Kᵀ√(dₖ)=frac 1√(2)begin bmatrix1&2&1&-1end bmatrix=begin bmatrixfrac 1√(2)&√(2)&frac 1√(2)&-frac 1√(2)end bmatrix
   Scaled dot-product attention divides the raw scores by \(\sqrt{d_k}\). Since \(d_k=2\), the divisor is \(\sqrt{2}\). Scaling helps prevent large dot products from making the softmax excessively concentrated.

5. Convert scores into attention weights with softmax
   αᵢ=frac e^widetilde sᵢ∑ⱼ=₁⁴e^widetilde sⱼ, α=softmax(widetilde s)
   Softmax converts the four real-valued scores into nonnegative weights that sum to one. The largest score, \(\sqrt{2}\), should receive the largest weight.

6. Evaluate the four attention weights
   α=frac 12e¹/√⁽²⁾+e√⁽²⁾+e⁻¹/√⁽²⁾begin bmatrixe¹/√⁽²⁾&e√⁽²⁾&e¹/√⁽²⁾&e⁻¹/√⁽²⁾end bmatrix≈begin bmatrix0.2341&0.4748&0.2341&0.0569end bmatrix
   The second token receives the greatest attention weight because its scaled similarity score is largest. The fourth token receives the least attention because its score is negative and smallest.

7. Verify that the weights form a probability-like distribution
   ∑ᵢ=₁⁴αᵢ=1, αᵢge 0
   The weights are all nonnegative and add to one. Therefore, they can be visualized as a heatmap or as four bars whose total height is one.

8. Form the attended representation as a weighted sum of values
   z₁=αV=∑ᵢ=₁⁴αᵢ vᵢ
   The attention output is not a single selected value. It is a weighted average of all four value vectors, with larger weights giving greater influence.

9. Compute the first coordinate of the attended vector
   z₁,₁=0.2341(1)+0.4748(2)+0.2341(-1)+0.0569(0)≈ 0.9497
   Multiply each attention weight by the first coordinate of its corresponding value vector, then add the four contributions.

10. Compute the second coordinate of the attended vector
   z₁,₂=0.2341(0)+0.4748(1)+0.2341(1)+0.0569(-1)≈ 0.6520
   Repeat the same weighted-sum calculation for the second coordinate of the value vectors.

11. Assemble and visualize the attended representation
   z₁=begin bmatrixz₁,₁\z ₁,₂end bmatrix≈begin bmatrix0.9497\\0.6520end bmatrix
   The final attended representation for the first token is a two-dimensional vector. The visualization can animate the process in three panels: raw or scaled scores, the softmax weight heatmap, and the value vectors being multiplied by those weights and summed.

12. State the general self-attention formula
   Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax (frac QKᵀ√(dₖ) )V
   For a complete sequence, every query produces one row of scores and one row of attention weights. Stacking all attended representations gives the standard scaled dot-product self-attention formula.

13. Final numerical result for the worked example
   z₁=frac e¹/√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix1\\0end bmatrix+e√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix2\\1end bmatrix+e¹/√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix-1\\1end bmatrix+e⁻¹/√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix0\\-1end bmatrix2e¹/√⁽²⁾+e√⁽²⁾+e⁻¹/√⁽²⁾≈begin bmatrix0.9497\\0.6520end bmatrix
   Thus, the query first compares itself with every key, softmax turns those similarities into weights \((0.2341,0.4748,0.2341,0.0569)\), and those weights combine the value vectors to produce the attended representation shown above.

Answer: z₁=frac e¹/√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix1\\0end bmatrix+e√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix2\\1end bmatrix+e¹/√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix-1\\1end bmatrix+e⁻¹/√⁽²⁾begin bmatrix0\\-1end bmatrix2e¹/√⁽²⁾+e√⁽²⁾+e⁻¹/√⁽²⁾≈begin bmatrix0.9497\\0.6520end bmatrix
For the first token, the scaled query-key scores are \(\left(1/\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2},1/\sqrt{2},-1/\sqrt{2}\right)\). Softmax converts them into attention weights \(\left(0.2341,0.4748,0.2341,0.0569\right)\). Applying these weights to the four value vectors gives the attended representation \(z_1\approx(0.9497,0.6520)\).

operations.title: The attention pipeline
operations.narration: Attention follows a simple pipeline. A query compares with every key, the scores become weights, and those weights blend the corresponding value vectors.

operations.title: Four tokens, three ingredients
operations.caption: n=4,\qquad d_k=2
operations.narration: We will update the first token. Its query is q_1, and it compares with four keys; each key has a matching value vector.

operations.title: Compare query with keys
operations.caption: q_1K^{\mathsf T}=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&1&-1\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: The query takes a dot product with each key. The four raw similarities are one, two, one, and negative one, so key two scores highest.

operations.title: Scale the scores
operations.caption: \widetilde{s}=\frac{q_1K^{\mathsf T}}{\sqrt{d_k}}
operations.narration: Because the key dimension is two, divide every score by the square root of two before applying softmax.

operations.title: Softmax turns scores into weights
operations.caption: \alpha_i=\frac{e^{\widetilde{s}_i}}{\sum_{j=1}^{4}e^{\widetilde{s}_j}}
operations.narration: Softmax exponentiates each scaled score and divides by the total of all four exponentials. The result is a set of nonnegative weights.

operations.title: The four attention weights
operations.caption: \boldsymbol{\alpha}\approx\begin{bmatrix}0.2341&0.4748&0.2341&0.0569\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: Evaluating softmax gives weights 0.2341, 0.4748, 0.2341, and 0.0569. The second token receives the most attention, while the fourth receives the least.

operations.title: Weights sum to one
operations.caption: \sum_{i=1}^{4}\alpha_i=1,\qquad \alpha_i\ge 0
operations.narration: Every weight is nonnegative, and together they add to one. That is why the values will be blended rather than arbitrarily scaled.

operations.title: Blend the value vectors
operations.caption: z_1=\boldsymbol{\alpha}V=\sum_{i=1}^{4}\alpha_i v_i
operations.narration: Attention does not choose just one value. It multiplies every value vector by its matching weight and adds all four contributions.

operations.title: First output coordinate
operations.caption: z_{1,1}=0.2341(1)+0.4748(2)+0.2341(-1)+0.0569(0)\approx 0.9497
operations.narration: For the first coordinate, multiply each attention weight by the corresponding first value coordinate. The contributions add to approximately 0.9497.

operations.title: Second output coordinate
operations.caption: z_{1,2}=0.2341(0)+0.4748(1)+0.2341(1)+0.0569(-1)\approx 0.6520
operations.narration: Repeat the same process for the second coordinate. The weighted contributions add to approximately 0.6520.

operations.title: Assemble the attended vector
operations.caption: z_1=\begin{bmatrix}z_{1,1}\\z_{1,2}\end{bmatrix}\approx\begin{bmatrix}0.9497\\0.6520\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: Put the two coordinates together. The first token's attended representation is approximately the vector 0.9497, 0.6520.

operations.title: The general formula
operations.caption: \operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\operatorname{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\mathsf T}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V
operations.narration: For a whole sequence, every query gets its own score row and weight row. Stacking the outputs gives the standard scaled dot-product attention formula.

operations.title: FINAL ANSWER
operations.caption: z_1\approx\begin{bmatrix}0.9497\\0.6520\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: For the first token, softmax gives weights 0.2341, 0.4748, 0.2341, and 0.0569. Their weighted combination of the four value vectors is the attended representation z_1, approximately the vector 0.9497, 0.6520.
